name: OIA Coral Reef Initiative and Natural Resources (CRNR) Program

funder.name: U.S. Department of the Interior, Office of Insular Affairs

summary: Federal grants to protect coral reefs and other natural resources and to fight invasive species in US territories and the freely associated states; the 2026 round has closed.

geography.label: U.S. insular areas and freely associated states

eligibility.rule: Government applicants are non-federal local entities or component units
Is not a judicial or legislative branch of a local government
Is not from a country supporting terrorism subject to U.S. sanctions
Is not from a U.S. Treasury-sanctioned country without licenses
Registered in SAM.gov before applying, unless applying as an individual

documents: SF-424A or SF-424C budget information form
Latest audit or financial capacity questions
Most recently negotiated indirect cost rate agreement, if applicable

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-federal, local government entities and component units, hospitals, health centers, institutions of higher education, and non-profit organizations in the United States and its territories

geography.quote: CRNR funds are available to benefit the U.S. territories of American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI), Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands (USVI) and the freely associated states

access.quote: Go to www.grants.gov to apply, track application status, and subscribe to updates.

effort.quote: Electronically submitted applications must be submitted no later than 11:59 PM, ET, on the listed application due date (the deadline has been extended to June 8, 2026).
During the eligibility review, the application is checked for timely submission, completed packages (see Application Documents above) and alignment with the requirements of this announcement.
The OIA Grant Management Specialists will review, score, and evaluate all eligible applications based on the Scoring Table in the Merit Review section.
Prior to making an award, the applicant will be assessed for their level of risk per 2 CFR 200.206.

eligibility.quote: non-federal, local government entities and component units
Judicial and legislative branches of local governments are not eligible per 2 CFR 200.444.
We do not fund countries supporting terrorism subject to U.S. sanctions.
We do not fund countries under U.S. Treasury sanctions without licenses.
Before applying, all applicants except individuals applying as a natural person must be registered in SAM.gov.

after_award.quote: A Performance Progress Report (PPR) and a Federal Financial Report (FFR) will be due semi-annually for the periods beginning January 1 and ending June 30 and beginning July 1 and ending December 31, throughout the grant period of performance.

documents.quote: SF-424 Application for Federal Assistance form o SF-424A Budget Information - Non-Construction Programs (Or SF-424C) o SF-424B Assurances - Non-Construction Programs (Or SF-424D) o Project Abstract • Complete Project Narrative

SF-424A, Budget Information - Non-Construction Programs Note: Applicants must fill out all pages of SF-424A, including the second page with the object class categories. Only required for nonconstruction projects SF-424C, Budget Information - Construction Programs

Project Abstract Summary, OMB No. 40400019 Must be only 1 page and include, in plain language: • • • • • Award purpose Activities to be performed Expected deliverables or outcomes Intended beneficiaries Subrecipient activities (if known at time of application) Required from all applicants Include Latest Audit or Answer Financial Capacity Questions
If your organization has previously negotiated a rate, attach a copy of the most recently negotiated rate agreement (active or expired).
